name: Displaying the Days That are Above 32 Degrees Fahrenheit
description: Construct a program that reads a series of temperatures and reports the days that are above 32 degrees Fahrenheit. Assume that the temperature values are in Fahrenheit. Also assume that input values could have a decimal point.
code:
#Step 1: Read the number of days that we have to enter their temperature data
num_days = int(input("Enter the number of temperature values that will be entered: "))
#Step 2: Read the temperature values
temps = []
for i in range(num_days):
    val = float(input("Enter the temperature: "))
    temps.append(val)
#Step 3: Create a list that contains the days that are above 32 degrees Fahrenheit
days_above_32 = []
for i in range(len(temps)) :
    if temps[i] > 32:
        days_above_32.append("Day " + str(i+1))
#Step 4: Print the result
print("Days above 32 degrees Fahrenheit:", days_above_32)

comments.content:
We need to first ask the user how many days of temperature data will be provided. To read the user input from command line, we use the input() function. This statement prints a text on the screen "Enter the number of temperature values that will be entered: ", then reads the text entered by the user.

The value that will be read is a string and we need to convert it to a int. We convert the input string to its integer representation by using the int() function.
Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from the input function in a variable. We could use the input function call directly as the int function parameter.

Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer.

We first need to define a list referred by variable temps for storing the temperatures that the user provides. We initialize it with an empty list and will later use the function append to add each temperature value to it. We need this list later to iterate through the temperature values and determine the days that are above 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

We want to read each temperature value and add each temperature value in the list to later determine the days that are above the average. Therefore, we use a for loop to iterate through the list indexes and add a temperature value to each index.

We need the list indexes to have a length of num_days and start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including num_days, where variable num_days is the number of days for which the user will provide the temperature values. We get this sequence by calling the range(num_days) function.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

We need to read the temperature value that the user enters. To read the user input from command line, we use the input() function. This statement prints a text on the screen "Enter the temperature: ", then reads the text entered by the user.

The value that will be read is a string and we need to convert it to a float. We convert the input string to its float representation by using the float() function.

The conversion of the value from string to float can only be done if the string could be translated into a valid floating-point value. Also note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from the input function in a variable. We could use the input function call directly as the float function parameter.
We want to add the temperature value that the user has entered to the list. To do this, in each iteration, we call the function append() to add the value read to the end of the list.

We first need to define a list referred by variable days_above_32 for storing the days that are above 32 degrees Fahrenheit. We initialize it with an empty list and will later use the function append to add days to it.

We want to iterate through the list of temperatures values and record the days that are above 32 degrees Fahrenheit. We need to iterate through the indexes in list of temperature values because the indexes in list represent the order that days were entered by the user; and thus, we can map each index to a day.

We can iterate through the list indexes using for loop because for loop can step across any kind of sequence object including lists. We need the list indexes to start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including the list size. We get this sequence by calling the range(len(temps) function.
Note that the function len(temps) returns the number of the values in the list. Also, note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

We need to compare the list value at index i with the threshold of 32 degrees Fahrenheit. If that value is greater than 32, then we need to add its corresponding day to the list referred by variable days_above_32.
If the list value at index i is greater than 32, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
When the temperature value at index i is greater than 32 degrees, we have to add its corresponding day to the list days_above_32. The value at index i corresponds to the temperature of (i+1)-th day.

We can concatenate the string "Day " and integer (i+1) by using the + operator. Note that when we want to concatenate an integer value with a string value, we need to explicitly convert the integer to a string value using the str function.
We use i+1 instead of i as the day number because day numbers start at 1 while the indexes of the list start at 0.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Days above 32 degrees Fahrenheit:" followed by the content of the list referred by variable days_above_32.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
Note that we can see the content of the list by calling the print function and passing the list to that.
